role: Senior Data Analyst (Analytics Engineering), Data Platform
responsibilities: Partner with Product, Engineering and business teams to turn their questions into analyses, metrics and data models.
Deliver analysis and reporting: ad hoc deep dives, recurring KPI reports and dashboards.
Define, validate and document KPIs with stakeholders, and help teams use them consistently in planning and decisions.
Build and maintain tested, documented data models and ELT transformations together with the Data Platform team.
Create curated datasets, dashboards and templates that let teams answer their own questions.
Take metrics and models from first prototype through production and ongoing maintenance.
Streamline analytics practices across analysts in other teams: shared modeling conventions, metric definitions, code review, and onboarding and coaching.
Prioritize requests from multiple teams, balancing urgent needs with investments in reusable data assets.
Identify gaps in data, instrumentation or tooling, and work with engineering to close them.
Present findings clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Build and maintain tested, documented data models
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: rigour terms ("reliable, reusable datasets", "tested, documented data models", "validate and document KPIs") dominate; "quick analysis" is framed as a judgement call, not a pace.
evidence.domain_risk: make internet connections safer for millions of homes
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: internal product and business analytics at a cybersecurity vendor, with no financial or regulatory reporting language, so moderate.
evidence.data_team_maturity: help scale analytics practices across the company
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: a Data Platform team exists and analysts sit in other teams, and the role scales and streamlines existing practices, so mid.
evidence.jd_authorship: Streamline analytics practices across analysts in other teams: shared modeling conventions, metric definitions, code review, and onboarding and coaching.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: the bullets name concrete practices such as "shared modeling conventions, metric definitions, code review", so a hiring manager wrote them.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: reliable, reusable datasets and metrics that teams across CUJO AI can use on their own
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: the emphasis is self-serve datasets and shared analytics practice for teams across the company, so internal_data.
evidence.autonomy_level: Define, validate and document KPIs...Deliver analysis and reporting
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: the role defines KPIs and analytics conventions while also delivering analysis to business teams, so mixed.
evidence.ai_role: Effective use of AI-assisted development tools
evidence.ai_role_explanation: the candidate is expected to use AI-assisted development tools on their own work (a stand-out item), so ai_user.
evidence.testing_framing: Build and maintain tested, documented data models
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: tested models are a responsibility the role owns, so responsibility.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: the ability to trace and fix issues upstream
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: reliability matters (reliable datasets, tracing issues upstream) but sits behind delivery, so moderate.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Take metrics and models from first prototype through production and ongoing maintenance.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: the role both builds new metrics and maintains them, so mixed.
evidence.language_gate: Strong verbal and written communication skills in English.
